questions.q: What distinguishes a dark pool from a public stock exchange?
options: A dark pool only trades commodities, not equities
A dark pool matches orders privately without displaying the order book before execution
A dark pool is regulated by a different country's government
A dark pool guarantees a better price than any exchange
questions.explain: Dark pools let institutions trade large blocks without publicly revealing their order before it executes, reducing the chance of moving the price against themselves.

questions.q: What is the key difference between a broker and a dealer?
options: A broker trades from its own account; a dealer never does
A broker acts as an agent executing trades for clients; a dealer acts as a principal trading its own account
There is no meaningful difference between the two terms
A dealer only operates in the bond market
questions.explain: A broker executes on a client's behalf for a commission without taking the other side; a dealer trades as a principal, taking on the position itself.

questions.q: Which best describes the buy-side vs. sell-side distinction?
options: Buy-side firms manage money and purchase securities; sell-side firms sell products and services like research and trade execution
Buy-side firms only trade bonds; sell-side firms only trade equities
Sell-side firms are always larger than buy-side firms
The terms refer to whether a firm is domestic or international
questions.explain: The buy-side (mutual funds, pension funds, hedge funds) manages money and buys securities. The sell-side (banks, broker-dealers, market makers) sells products and services to the buy-side.

questions.q: Why does a market maker earn the bid-ask spread?
options: It is a fee set by government regulation
As compensation for continuously standing ready to trade and bearing inventory and information risk
It is paid directly by the exchange as a subsidy
It only applies to retail investors, not institutions
questions.explain: The bid-ask spread compensates the market maker for the risk of holding inventory and the risk of trading against better-informed counterparties while providing continuous liquidity.

questions.q: What does a central counterparty (CCP) accomplish through novation?
options: It sets the opening price for the trading day
It inserts itself between the original buyer and seller so each faces the CCP's credit risk instead of each other's
It replaces brokers entirely in the trading process
It determines which asset class a security belongs to
questions.explain: Through novation, the clearinghouse becomes the seller to the original buyer and the buyer to the original seller, guaranteeing settlement even if one original party defaults.
